sections.html:
Go to room 400 of the Courthouse, 625 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, TN 37402. Doors are open Monday through Friday, eight to four, and shut on county holidays. The phone number is 423-209-6560.

By statute (Tenn. Code Ann. 66-24-101) the register records deeds and other instruments the law allows, then collects and accounts for the fees and taxes attached to them. Plats, powers of attorney, mortgages and military discharges all go through the same counter. When a Hamilton County house sells, the deed for that sale ends up here. The office posts notices and links on its home page, and it is worth a look before you file anything by hand.

Most sellers never need to visit. The title company or closing attorney carries the deed over, pays the fees and taxes, and files electronically if it uses one of the vendors listed below. If you do go yourself, bring the signed and notarized deed, a way to pay the filing fee and tax, and any exemption language your transfer relies on. Staff can answer questions about what the office will accept.

Recording a standard deed of two pages or fewer is $12.00, which includes a $2.00 data processing fee. Add $5.00 for every extra page. Taxes are billed in addition to filing fees.

Before you send a check, run the amounts through the office's online fee calculator, which is linked from the register's home page.

Plan for the total, not just the base fee. A deed that runs long adds a charge for each extra page, and each taxable document carries the small extra fee shown in the table. Your title company usually adds these up for you and lists them on the settlement statement, but if you file yourself, bring a check large enough to cover the fee, the tax and the extras, and ask the counter to confirm the figure before you hand over the deed.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Hamilton County home sale
sections.html:
State realty transfer tax runs 37 cents per $100 of the tax base. It is the named grantee's bill, collected at filing by the register in the county where the deed is offered. Deeds of trust carry a mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 after the first $2,000.

  • As a rule the base is whichever is higher, price paid or value.
  • Revenue officials take the assessor's listed value, or a recent appraisal the assessor accepted, as fair market value. A lower figure invites an audit.
  • A genuine quitclaim deed is taxed on what was paid. If the wording conveys the property itself, such as a habendum clause or "in fee simple," tax is due on market value.

Your contract may allocate the cost differently, so read it and compare with the settlement statement before closing.

Many family and estate transfers escape the tax, and the Department of Revenue's recordation tax help center names each. Staff at the register can tell you what exemption wording they expect on your deed.

  • Real estate moved between spouses.
  • A property adjustment ordered in a divorce.
  • A transfer under a will, called a testamentary devise.
  • Transfers under a revocable living trust, and the release of a life estate.
  • A division in kind between tenants in common.
  • Transfers to government entities.

A deed on death is not recognized in Tennessee, so a document of that type cannot be recorded in Hamilton County. Inherited a house? Phone first and ask what the office will take.

Since April 27, 2026, an affidavit offered for recording in Tennessee needs two separate statements, each with its own notary. The change comes from an amendment to Tenn. Code Ann. 66-24-101, and the Hamilton County register posts it as a standing notice.

  1. A jurat under 66-24-101(g) that swears the contents are true. The register must reject the document if it is missing.
  2. An acknowledgment, or two witnesses, under 66-22-101 confirming that each signer is who they claim to be.
  3. Both statements are needed for every signature on the document.

If you record an affidavit of heirship, a correction affidavit or a similar paper before closing, have the notary read this notice first.

Electronic filers are pointed to two vendors. Simplifile answers at (800) 460-5657. Corporation Service Company is at (866) 652-0111 or eRecording.com. Ask your title company whether it submits that way.

Searching the database online is a separate step. You complete a print or online application, and the $50 fee, plus a monthly access fee, must be paid before passwords go out. The office also publishes an instructions PDF for the record search, a document requirement guide, a public records policy and request form, and a monthly report of the property transactions recorded the month before.

Need a single deed? Certified copies run $1.00 a page for deeds and $5.00 a page for plats. Call 423-209-6560 for questions about a specific instrument.

sections.h2: Property tax after the deed is recorded
sections.html:
Recording a deed does not settle the tax bill. From the register's pages you can reach three tools: the Assessor of Property, the Trustee's online property search, and Chattanooga's property tax site, where bills from both governments can be searched and paid. No registration is needed to look up a bill on the Chattanooga site.

If your house is in Chattanooga, expect both a county and a city bill. If it is in another part of the county, ask the Trustee which municipal bill, if any, applies. Have the title company run both searches before closing, so any unpaid tax comes out of your proceeds instead of following the house.

The county spans 576 square miles of southeast Tennessee. Chattanooga is the seat, on the Tennessee River, with Georgia to the south. Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy-Daisy, Lookout Mountain, Signal Mountain and Walden are the other incorporated places.

The county had 390,833 residents in 2025, up from 366,207 in 2020. About 63.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, rent is a median $1,253 and household income is a median $76,183.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Hamilton County register?
faqs.a: Call 423-209-6560 or fax 423-209-6561. Visit room 400 at 625 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, weekdays eight to four.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Hamilton County deed?
faqs.a: The grantee, meaning the buyer, owes it at $0.37 per $100, collected at filing. Your contract may split the cost another way.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed on death in Hamilton County?
faqs.a: No. Tennessee does not recognize deeds on death, so they cannot be recorded. For an inherited property, ask the office what it accepts.

faqs.q: Does Hamilton County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The register names two vendors, Simplifile at (800) 460-5657 and Corporation Service Company at (866) 652-0111. Your title company can tell you whether it files electronically.

faqs.q: What is the charge for a certified deed copy?
faqs.a: Certified deed copies cost $1.00 a page and certified plats $5.00 a page. Plain copies are $0.15 a page. The fee calculator confirms current amounts.
